paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : MMLU confidence vs. accuracy

annotations.annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and different measures of Accuracy (Final Accuracy, ∆ Accuracy, Initial Accuracy). The x-axis represents "Initial Confidence" on a linear scale, ranging from 0.86 to 1.00, with tick labels at intervals of 0.01 except that 0.87 is missing. The y-axis represents "Accuracy," also on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The blue line, representing "Final Accuracy", uses circle markers and a solid line style. It starts at approximately 0.9 and remains consistently high around this value across the x-axis, finally finishing at around 0.99 for an x-value of 1. The orange line, denoting "∆ Accuracy", features diamond markers and a dashed line style, beginning near 0.3 at 0.86 and displaying a slight decline to around 0.10 around 0.95, then fluctuating slightly afterwards and finally finishing around 0.2. The green line, indicating "Initial Accuracy", uses square markers with a dashed line style. It starts at about 0.65, showing a gradual increase to around 0.95 before decreasing slightly towards the final value of the x-axis. All three lines include error bars, indicating variability at each data point. There are legends provided on top of the plot to match different line styles to their labels.
